newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico needs better ag trade mechanisms - Labastida.
newsitem.headline: Mexico needs better ag trade mechanisms - Labastida.

text.p: Mexico's Agriculture Minister Francisco Labastida Ochoa recognised Thursday that the country needs improved trading mechanisms for farm products.

"In Mexico, we need to construct a trading system capable of absorbing harvests with corresponding remunerative prices...for the benefit of consumers and farmers," Labastida said according to a statement from the ministry.
Labastida said federal and state governments and farmers themselves should have roles in the improved trading mechanisms.

"Together, we have to look for a mixture of resources so that the trading system improves, develops capacity to buy crops and results in profitable prices for growers," he said, without adding any indication of government initiatives.

Mexico's current agricultural product trading is ad hoc and the sector is underpinned by government subsidies doled out to farmers and policies of minimum floor prices for basic products, such as corn.
No formal agricultural exchanges exist, although most farmers agree there is a need for more formal trading practices for greater price transparency.
Labastida said domestic white corn floor prices are between 1,200 and 1,250 pesos per tonne, although slightly higher in some states, which is about 50 percent more expensive than U.S. market prices.

Labastida said this high level of floor prices was possible because of funds supplied from federal and some state governments, although he stressed Mexico's agricultural subsidy policy was congruent with norms established by the World Trade Organisation.
